chase_cards.name: Tropical Present
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is not only a card but a receipt of club participation: the Summer 2001 Tropical Present turns GET Points, mail, postcard scale, and an e-card-era visual edge into one object.

key_artists.name: Hiromi Ito
key_artists.why: Ito matters here because the 2001 print is the third Tropical Present identity, not a generic reprint. Bulbapedia also credits Ito with logo work on Tropical Mega Battle Trainer cards, which keeps his trace close to the tournament/gift-card visual apparatus rather than ordinary Pokemon portraiture.

claims.text: The local catalog models Pokemon Card Fan Club (Summer 2001) as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Tropical Present at source index 236, with Postcard as the variant note.
Bulbapedia says the Summer 2001 Tropical Present was sent to Pokemon Fan Club members who had already earned 200 GET Points or more.
Bulbapedia says Tropical Present's card text states the special card was sent to players to obtain 10 GET Points, with points added automatically.
Bulbapedia identifies the Summer 2001 Tropical Present print as illustrated by Hiromi Ito.
Bulbapedia's Hiromi Ito page lists Tropical Present under cards illustrated and credits Ito with logo work on Tropical Mega Battle No.1 Trainer, No.2 Trainer, and No.3 Trainer cards.

Bulbapedia says Tropical Present had three Japanese Fan Club versions: an early 1999 Atsuko Nishida print, a July/Summer 1999 Naoyo Kimura print using Southern Islands Sea-scene artwork, and a Summer 2001 e-card-stock print with new artwork by Hiromi Ito.

Bulbapedia says the e-card reprint has '2001/Summer' where a collection number usually appears and uses the Pokemon Fan Club logo in place of an expansion symbol, with the logo replacing the e on the e-card reprint.
Bulbapedia identifies Tropical Present as Japanese トロピカルプレゼント, translated Tropical Present, a Special Card and Unnumbered Promotional card that was never released in English.

As judged collector texture, the Summer 2001 Tropical Present matters because the same Fan Club title becomes a new assembly: higher GET threshold, e-card-era stock/marking, new Hiromi Ito artwork, and the same gift-card function of turning membership activity into a physical object.

Agents should preserve the Summer 2001 Fan Club route, source index 236, postcard/Jumbo/Special Card format, 200 GET Points threshold, 2001/Summer marking, e-card-stock edge, Fan Club logo treatment, Hiromi Ito art credit, and non-equivalence with the 1999 Tropical Present prints before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present, Summer 2001: the Fan Club ledger becomes a postcard again
narrative.why_it_matters: Tropical Present is a beautiful little lesson in Pokemon's social machinery. It looks like a card, but it behaves like club infrastructure: a mailed object, a Jumbo postcard, a Special Card, a little automatic credit back into the GET Points account. By 2001 the same title has become an e-card-era artifact with Hiromi Ito art and a 2001/Summer tell. That is why the catalog has to love it carefully. The word Tropical is not the identity; the route is.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify Summer 2001 Tropical Present by Fan Club route, postcard/Jumbo/Special Card format, e-card-stock 2001/Summer marking, Fan Club logo treatment, Hiromi Ito artwork, and 200 GET Points context before trusting the repeated Tropical Present title.
steps: Confirm the exact title pair: Tropical Present / トロピカルプレゼント.
Confirm the route is Pokemon Card Fan Club Summer 2001, local source index 236, not January 1999 or July/Summer 1999.
Confirm the object is a postcard / Jumbo / Special Card object rather than a standard-size Trainer card.
Look for the e-card-stock identity and the '2001/Summer' marking where a collection number would usually appear.
Check the Pokemon Fan Club logo treatment, including its replacement of the e-card e on this reprint.
Preserve Hiromi Ito as the Summer 2001 illustrator; separate Atsuko Nishida's early 1999 print and Naoyo Kimura's Summer 1999 Southern Islands Sea-scene print.

Separate this row from Southern Islands set cards, Tropical Mega Battle / Tropical Wind material, ordinary Trainer cards, and generic tropical-themed listings unless the seller evidence proves this exact Fan Club object.

For a transaction, require seller-controlled front/back photos plus size evidence, postcard/Jumbo context, logo/marking close-ups, surface/corner evidence, and slab label/cert if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Present 2001: a card-shaped thank-you from the Fan Club
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of those objects that makes the catalog feel alive. It is not a battle card in the normal way. It is a club thank-you, a point-bank nudge, a mailed Jumbo thing, and by 2001 it even wears the e-card era on its body. Hiromi Ito gives the final Tropical Present print its own face, but the deeper charm is social: a collector did something, the Fan Club noticed, and a present arrived.
